articles.title: Italian GP: George Russell fastest in Practice Two as Mercedes edge ahead of fast-starting Ferrari at Monza
articles.summary: George Russell starts a big weekend in which Kimi Antonelli takes a grid penalty by setting Friday's fastest time at The Temple of Speed; Charles Leclerc leads Ferrari in second; watch final practice at 11.30am on Saturday ahead of Qualifying at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
At an event in which championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli will start at the back of Sunday's grid owing to engine-change penalties, Russell has a big chance to eat into the Italian's 59-point advantage if he can deliver a strong race weekend.

Ferrari had finished first and second quickest in opening practice as they debuted an upgraded engine but Russell was the driver to beat in the second session amid continued sweltering temperatures in northern Italy.

The Briton set a quickest lap of 1:22.559 to outpace Leclerc - who had a late spin - by 0.120s and Antonelli by 0.141s.

Lewis Hamilton, second fastest in the earlier running, slipped to fifth behind McLaren's Lando Norris during a session which included the Ferrari running straight on at the first chicane.

Norris has won the last two races but McLaren are expecting Monza's straights and slow chicanes to prove more challenging for their car. Fourth-fastest Norris was 0.384s off the second-practice pace with Oscar Piastri a further tenth behind in sixth.

The world champion was angered by what he perceived to be "dangerous" driving by Aston Martin's Lance Stroll midway through the session when he was forced off track at the first chicane. That incident was placed under a post-session stewards' investigation.

Max Verstappen returned after sitting out the first session for Red Bull rookie Ayumu Iwasa but the Dutchman was unhappy with his RB22's balance and was only able to set the ninth-fastest time. Stand-in team-mate Liam Lawson was 12th.

Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad was the leading Red Bull-owned car in seventh place, with Haas' Oliver Bearman eighth in an upgraded VF-26 car.

'This is his big chance' - Russell makes ideal start at Monza

While he certainly will not be getting carried away by setting the Friday pace, Russell has clearly got his weekend off to a positive start ahead of his bids for a first Grand Prix pole and win since the Austrian Grand Prix five events ago.

Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle said: "He looked good. This is his big chance to close that deficit this weekend and show that he is very worthy of a world championship.

"What he desperately doesn't want to have to do is fall into line a few races down the road and protect Kimi Antonelli if there's an onslaught coming from McLaren or Ferrari at his championship lead.

"These are key races now for George Russell."

Antonelli, meanwhile, knows his weekend is already compromised given he will start from likely the back row of Sunday's 22-car grid. His programme on Friday was therefore more heavily weighted towards long-run pace.

"Today a bit of a different day compared to usual," said Antonelli.

"A lot more focused on long runs so it was a bit weird - not going to lie - but overall, it was a good day. We gathered a lot of data and now looking forward to the next few days."

Monza's long straights offer overtaking opportunities and Antonelli said he learnt lots from following other cars.

"It's a track where you can do so many different things," he added.

"It was interesting in the long run today running behind other cars to see what they were doing differently, where they were deploying compared to us. So it was very interesting. We have gathered a lot of data and now we look forward to tomorrow."

articles.title: Sainz, reticente con los rebufos: "A mí me distraen más que me ayudan"
articles.standfirst: Carlos, relativamente satisfecho con el Williams el viernes en Monza, donde "estuvimos probando cosas interesantes para el futuro"
articles.summary: Carlos, relativamente satisfecho con el Williams el viernes en Monza, aunque reconoce que
articles.body: Volver a superar a Aston Martin en una pista como Monza, gracias al motor Mercedes y a una mejor velocidad punta, era algo esperado, aunque quizá no tanto como acabar con 1,1 segundos de ventaja sobre Fernando Alonso, algo impensable desde Hungría. Carlos Sainz acabó 17º en Libres 2, a un paso de un hipotético paso a la Q2 del sábado, aunque el madrileño reconocía que afinar para la mejor vuelta en Monza no había sido su prioridad en toda la jornada. "Estuvo bien, aunque no le doy mucha importancia a los viernes ahora mismo, porque estamos probando cosas muy diferentes en el coche para intentar encontrar ideas para el año que viene. Así que, aprovechando que no había sprint el viernes, hicimos una pequeña sesión de pruebas y dejamos el coche en una posición más básica para mañana", relataba. Sobre el efecto de esos test, Carlos era positivo: "Sí, estamos probando cosas interesantes que nos dan información para el año que viene y, probablemente, sacrificamos un poco el fin de semana en ese sentido, pero creo que será interesante para el futuro", valoraba. En cuanto a la incidencia del rebufo en Monza y a si lo intentará con Alex Albon en la qualy del sábado, Sainz no lo tenía nada claro. "La verdad es que personalmente siempre encuentro que el rebufo distrae más que ayuda, así que no soy muy fan. Simplemente porque no puedo concentrarme en mi vuelta de clasificación con un coche demasiado cerca delante... no sé cómo lo hacen los de F2, pero sin duda experimentaremos con ello e intentaremos encontrar el equilibrio adecuado", dice, concediendo que lo intentarán, como casi todos los equipos en la cronometrada oficial de mañana.

articles.title: Andrea Stella says allegations from Alpine chief Flavio Briatore are 'insulting' for McLaren after court rules on Monaco podium
articles.summary: Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar restored to third in Monaco GP after Alpine driver Pierre Gasly’s time penalties were reapplied; McLaren and Red Bull won case at FIA's International Court of Appeal; watch Italian GP Qualifying live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm on Saturday
articles.body:
The court announced on Friday that penalties given to Alpine driver Pierre Gasly during June's Monaco Grand Prix would be reinstated, following a successful appeal by McLaren and Red Bull.

Gasly took the chequered flag in third but was demoted when two five-second penalties for speeding in the pit lane were applied at that point. However, a right of review appeal from Alpine saw the penalties withdrawn five days later.

The reinstatement of the penalty drops Gasly back to seventh in the official classification. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar gets a podium in third, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri moves up to fourth.

In an explosive press conference at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, which coincidentally featured Alpine executive director Briatore and McLaren team principal Stella, the pair engaged in a remarkable clash.

Alpine had put out a statement moments after the decision was announced expressing "disappointment" with the outcome but also said that the team "acknowledges the decision of the judging panel from the recent hearing in Paris".

Briatore stunned the room by striking a different tone in the press conference just a couple of hours later as he complained that one of the four judges at the hearing had a "working relationship" with McLaren.

"I think it's very unfair, firstly, but we accept the decision," Briatore said. "But what is very strange was the third judge in the panel, one of the judges acted like a prosecutor.

"For this, not a big problem. The problem is, he is very linked with the McLaren company."

Briatore pointed to the individual's presence at a charity event in California in 2018, at which he claimed "two of three McLaren cars" were donated.

"We have a nice picture of this guy at the speech for McLaren in 2018," Briatore said.

"I think it was quite unfair that one of the judges was linked with a team protesting us."

Briatore added that the judge in question was "very nasty" to Alpine's representatives during the hearing, and said that his team were "thinking about" taking legal action.

The FIA has yet to formally respond to Briatore's comments but Sky Sports News understands the sport's governing body is confident in the independence of its International Court of Appeal and the process for selecting its panel of judges.

Stella: McLaren deserve a lot of respect

Stella initially chose not to respond to Briatore's comments, but eventually appeared to threaten his fellow Italian with legal action.

"I find that this conference is going in this direction quite insulting for McLaren, for the reputation of a team that deserves a lot of respect," Stella said.

"And if anybody makes this kind of allegations, which seem quite serious, they are going to have to take the responsibility for what they are saying in a public forum.

"The hearing, the whole international court of appeal was conducted to the highest standards. We should not question this space, like it's been done."

Stella has insisted throughout the process that McLaren were more interested in clarifying the rules for the good of the sport, rather than gaining two points for Piastri, who is not in championship contention this season.

"We had concerns which were beyond the fact that we might have lost two championship points, probably these two points aren't going to make any difference," Stella said.

"We were concerned about the application of sporting equality and fairness, and this is important. And this is not only important for McLaren.

"Not only Red Bull applied, but all teams were present in the hearing because this was a very important moment in terms of clarification as to how we apply the rules, as to how we apply consistency.

"And also, in this specific case, consistencies that are related to the methodologies that are valid throughout our race weekend."

Alpine won their right of review case after presenting evidence which the stewards agreed was a "significant and relevant new element" regarding an incorrect distance calculation in the pit lane, showing the Frenchman was in fact not speeding.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes' George Russell (whose penalty was later converted into a drive-through) and McLaren's Piastri were all hit by the same speeding sanction, but as the drivers had already served the penalties during the race they could not be undone.
